title: [Python][FlightRPC] Tests segfault on OSX in conda-forge
body: The conda-forge macOS test suite has had to skip the PyArrow Flight tests because they segfault. I retried with Arrow 13.0.0, and the failure remains in the first test in test_flight.py: test_flight_client_close terminates Python with a segmentation fault. This is potentially serious because the whole Flight module may be unusable on macOS in the conda packages.

symptoms_visible: With Arrow 13.0.0 in the conda-forge macOS build, Python terminates with a segmentation fault when the suite reaches test_flight.py::test_flight_client_close.
N0.label: N0 conda macOS Flight segfault reported

symptoms_visible: The conda macOS Flight tests also segfaulted with Arrow 10 and 11, although the particular Flight test at which the suite stopped was not always the same.
N1.label: N1 earlier failures and possible leads collected

symptoms_visible: The Flight tests complete on native arm64, but the x86_64 conda environment under Rosetta intermittently terminates with EXC_BAD_ACCESS; even an individual test only fails on some runs.
N2.label: N2 architecture-specific intermittent crash reproduced

symptoms_visible: With the server running separately and serving indefinitely, repeated client runs still crash at random with EXC_BAD_ACCESS.
The debugger stops in libgrpc while StatusGetChildren is copying an Abseil Cord whose recorded representation is 0x1.
N3.label: N3 crash isolated and debug backtrace captured

symptoms_visible: The rebuilt conda packages run the full PyArrow test suite without errors, including the Flight tests that previously segfaulted.
N4.label: N4 candidate dependency rebuild verified

symptoms_visible: After the conda dependency update, the complete PyArrow test suite runs without errors on macOS and the Flight tests no longer segfault.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after Abseil upgrade

question_patterns: Did the same conda macOS failure occur with earlier Arrow releases?
Is this new in Arrow 13, or did previous packaged versions also crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I saw the same kind of segfault on osx-64 with Arrow 10 and 11. At that time it stopped in test_flight_list_flights rather than the Arrow 13 test_flight_client_close failure.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Arrow 10 through 12 all pass; the crash appeared only after updating to Arrow 13.
Arrow 10 and 11 also crash, but the first failing Flight test varies between runs.

question_patterns: Did you find any existing issue or source-code comment that might be relevant?
Are there any prior clues about this segfault in the Flight tests or packaging dependencies?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I had noted conda-forge/grpc-cpp-feedstock issue 281 as potentially related. The ConstantFlightServer test utility also has a comment saying it will segfault if Flight does not properly hold a reference to the Table object, although I don't know whether that is the cause here.

edges.comment: Reporter follow-ups c2-c3: the reporter supplied the Arrow 10/11 history, the grpc-cpp feedstock issue, and the cautionary Table-reference comment as possible leads, without claiming either was the cause.

question_patterns: Can the packaged Flight tests be run on a native arm64 Mac, and what is the raw result?
Does the same test package crash when run natively on Apple Silicon?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the Flight tests manually on native aarch64. The result was 63 passed and 9 skipped in 106.74 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The native arm64 run also terminates with the same intermittent EXC_BAD_ACCESS.
The native arm64 run passes with the same skips but takes a little longer.

question_patterns: Can you run the x86_64 package under Rosetta and report whether the crash reproduces consistently?
What happens if you repeat an individual Flight test in an x64 environment on that Mac?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It crashes under Rosetta in an x86_64 environment. The failure is random: repeatedly running an individual test only fails some of the time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The x86_64 Rosetta suite also passes every time; I cannot reproduce the crash outside the original CI worker.

edges.comment: Participant3 measurements c5-c8 are folded into the simulated user side: the reporter supplied the package-testing instructions, and the maintainer tester produced the native arm64 and Rosetta x86_64 results on the same Apple Silicon machine.

question_patterns: Can you separate the server from the test process and repeatedly run only a client against it?
Does the crash still occur if the server remains alive instead of being shut down by the test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I split the server into a separate file and left it serving forever. Repeated client runs against it still crash randomly with the same stack trace.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the server in a separate process, repeated client runs never crash; it only fails while the in-process server is being destroyed.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this with a debug build and paste the relevant debugger frames?
Where does LLDB stop when the intermittent EXC_BAD_ACCESS occurs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: LLDB stops in libgrpc.33.0.0.dylib in grpc_core::StatusGetChildren while incrementing an Abseil Cord refcount. The frames show CordRep::Ref with rep=0x1 and RefcountAndFlags::Increment with this=0x9.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug backtrace stops in PyArrow while releasing the Table owned by ConstantFlightServer, before entering any gRPC or Abseil frame.
The thread number and addresses vary, but every captured crash has the same StatusGetChildren and Abseil Cord frames in libgrpc.

edges.comment: Participant3 investigation c8-c27, folded as technical user-side measurements. The answer preserves the raw isolation result and debugger frames. The conclusion that this implicates the conda gRPC/Abseil dependency interaction rather than Flight object retention is reserved for the final solution inference.

question_patterns: Can you test the rebuilt packages from the feedstock change and report the complete test-suite result?
Please run the previously failing Flight tests using the candidate conda packages and tell me what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the rebuilt packages from the feedstock PR. The full PyArrow test suite runs without errors, and the Flight tests no longer segfault.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The rebuilt packages still intermittently segfault in the same Flight tests with the same libgrpc stack trace.
The complete suite passes twice, with only the existing expected skips differing between runs.

edges.comment: Reporter resolution evidence c31 and c35: the candidate arrow-cpp feedstock rebuild used an upgraded Abseil and completed the full suite. The dependency change is recorded as target-node volunteered information; the clarification answer itself is the raw test outcome.

solution.intent: Update and rebuild the conda-forge Arrow and gRPC dependency stack with the newer Abseil package, since the intermittent x86 macOS crash is in gRPC's handling of an Abseil Cord and disappears after that dependency upgrade.
solution.concrete_example: Adopt the tested conda-forge recipe update that upgrades Abseil and rebuild the affected packages; the candidate arrow-cpp feedstock build then runs the complete PyArrow suite without the Flight segfault.
solution.inference_hint: The raw evidence establishes an intermittent x86_64/Rosetta crash inside libgrpc while manipulating an invalid Abseil Cord, persistence with the server isolated, and successful full-suite testing after an Abseil upgrade. Concluding that the conda gRPC/Abseil dependency interaction—not Flight's Table-reference lifetime—is the accepted root cause is engineer-side synthesis.

edges.comment: Final accepted resolution from reporter c31 and c35: upgrading Abseil in the conda-forge package stack removed the segfault, and the complete suite passed. The later dylib-linkage warning was treated as a separate likely packaging-check false positive and is deliberately excluded from this diagnostic chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause at the level established by the thread: the conda macOS crash was tied to the packaged gRPC/Abseil interaction and resolved by upgrading Abseil, rather than by changing PyArrow Flight's Table ownership.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: native arm64 passed, x86_64 under Rosetta crashed intermittently, the crash persisted with a separate long-running server, and LLDB stopped in libgrpc while manipulating an invalid Abseil Cord.
Must recommend upgrading Abseil and rebuilding or adopting the updated conda packages, not treating skipped Flight tests as an acceptable permanent workaround.
Must not pursue the ConstantFlightServer Table-reference comment as the final fix; it was judged a red herring and does not explain the isolated-client gRPC backtrace.
Must have the rebuilt packages run the previously failing Flight tests or full PyArrow suite successfully before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical conda-forge package maintainer familiar with Arrow packaging, feedstock CI, conda-build artifacts, dependency versions, CMake, LLDB output, and cross-architecture macOS testing.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, collaborative, and evidence-driven; links prior packaging changes, quotes exact logs and source comments, offers CI assistance, and distinguishes confirmed test results from tentative hypotheses.
